definitions.gloss: mallet; hammer (with a wooden or metal head)
definitions.explanation: A striking tool with a heavy head fixed at right angles to a handle, used to drive chisels, stakes, and pegs or to pound materials. The head may be wood or metal.

examples.english: Drive a stake in with a mallet.

examples.japanese: ⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{槌|つち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{振|ふ}り{下|お}ろした。
examples.english: The craftsman brought the hammer down.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鍛冶屋|かじや}→鍛冶屋：26011_kajiya⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{槌|つち}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{熱|あつ}い→熱い：09888_atsui⟧⟦{鉄|てつ}→鉄：02225_tetsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{叩|たた}いて→叩く：02072_tataku⟧⟦{形|かたち}→形：02193_katachi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: Blacksmiths of old shaped hot iron by striking it with a hammer.

notes:
A somewhat literary or trade term; in everyday speech ⟦ハンマー→ハンマー：25887_hanmaa⟧ or ⟦{金槌|かなづち}→金槌：05476_kanazuchi⟧ (metal-headed hammer) is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {槌|つち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{振|ふ}るう→振るう：12793_furuu⟧: to wield a mallet
- {槌|つち}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧: to strike with a mallet
- ⟦{木槌|きづち}→木槌：29979_kizuchi⟧: wooden mallet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{金槌|かなづち}→金槌：05476_kanazuchi⟧: metal hammer — also the everyday word for someone who cannot swim
- ⟦ハンマー→ハンマー：25887_hanmaa⟧: hammer — the common katakana loanword
